prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, through ligand design and mechanistic understanding of C-N bond formation.

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from B046 to B004. The reasons are the ones I would apply to any claim in my own field: independent reproduction, a defined chemical reaction, and a case that does not depend on future results. Pd-catalysed C-N coupling meets all three. The reaction is defined (amine binding, deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination), the ligand solution is general, and it has been reproduced for about thirty years in laboratories that have no connection to the originators, in medicinal chemistry, process chemistry and materials. Somfai and Zou answered my opening worry about the 2010 prize on the merits. The difficulty with C-N bond formation was a different mechanistic problem, not a corollary of C-C coupling, and the ligand toolbox that solved it is what the prize would recognise. Attribution is a clean pair, Buchwald and Hartwig, who independently built the catalytic version. Kosugi's tin-amide reaction used stoichiometric toxic tin reagents with narrow scope, so I keep him off the list as a precursor, which also leaves the third slot unused instead of padded.
statement.case_against: The overlap with the 2010 prize is not zero. A reader can still see this as completing a recognised field, and it is the most conventional prize on the list. Kosugi's priority could be challenged if the citation is written loosely, so the wording must say catalytic, general and ligand-controlled. B004 is also less novel in principle than B046 or B040, and if the committee wants a new modality this year it will find this configuration conservative. I hold that cost to be smaller than the risk of a configuration that is premature (B046) or whose names cannot be agreed (B040).

responses.point: Somfai argued that C-N coupling needed a different mechanistic solution from the 2010 C-C prize (amine binding, deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination, suppression of beta-hydride elimination and catalyst deactivation), and that the general direct amine coupling, not Kosugi's tin reagent, is what chemists use.
responses.response: This is the argument that moved me. In round 1 I treated the overlap with 2010 as a mark against novelty. The distinction you draw is about the chemical reaction, and that is how I judge things: the rate and selectivity problems are different, the ligand classes are different, and the enabling effect is independently reproduced across a very wide substrate range. I accept it and I now rank B004 first. I agree on Kosugi: the general catalytic method is the discovery, and the precursor can be noted in the report text, not in the laureate list.

responses.point: Zou asked that the report documents state explicitly that Kosugi's stoichiometric tin reagents did not give a general method, so that the citation reads as the general catalytic method and is protected from a priority challenge.
responses.response: I support that. A citation that says catalytic, general and ligand-controlled is accurate and protects the prize. I would ask the reports to confirm one factual point, that independent groups reproduced the Buchwald and Hartwig catalysts and not only the originators, since reproduction outside the originating groups is my main test. I read the record that way, but I rely on recollection and want the report to confirm it. I also take your caution about a split configuration: with B004 at two names, the cap leaves room for no second part.

responses.point: Aqvist argued that what changed in vivo outcomes was the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid (MacLachlan and Cullis, then Anderson's lipidoid libraries), not the earlier liposome and remote-loading formulation of Hope and Madden, so the credit should follow the ionizable-lipid design.
responses.response: Your argument is chemically sound and it weakens my opening Cullis, Madden and Hope trio, which I now regard as the less defensible of the two. I still cannot settle priority between the Vancouver formulation lineage and the lipidoid lineage from memory, and neither can any other member who has spoken, so that is the reason B040 does not become my first choice. Hope and Madden would be left out, and so would Langer, and a prize that depends on that arbitration is fragile now. I keep B040 as an alternative and would support it if the reports settle who first showed the principle in vivo.

responses.point: Aili moved B040 ahead of B046 because no designed PROTAC is approved and the credit between PROTAC inventors and cereblon discoverers is not a clean three-person split, and he keeps B046 as his first alternative.
responses.response: I agree with your downgrade and it settles the chair's question to me. I do not consider B046 ready this year. The cereblon mechanism is well reproduced, but the clinical case is prospective, Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim fall outside three names, and two lineages share one citation only by stretching it. I still think induced proximity is a real chemical principle and I keep B046 as an alternative for a later year. I also withdraw my suggestion in round 1 that the case could stand on mechanism alone, since a mechanism-only citation would favour Handa and under-credit the PROTAC designers.

responses.point: Linke asked whether the committee wants a second computational prize after 2013 and 2024 and a delivery prize soon after the 2023 Medicine mRNA prize, and how much weight either recency consideration should carry.
responses.response: I give recency little weight in either direction, but it is not zero. A delivery prize shortly after 2023 is easier to defend than a third computational prize, because the lipid chemistry was left out in 2023, so that argument does not decide between B040 and B004. It does count against B021. The risk comparison you asked for is where I land: I prefer the mature method with a clean pair to the newer modality with a contested trio, because I can state B004's attribution and reproducibility from the record and cannot do that for B040.

uncertainties: Whether the reports confirm that Buchwald's and Hartwig's catalysts were reproduced by independent groups at scale, which I assume from recollection.
How much the committee will treat the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize as a bar, which could still decide the vote against B004.
Whether the reports resolve who first demonstrated the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid in vivo; if they do, B040 could become competitive.
Whether Kosugi should be named in the citation text or left to the report.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi, and no recusal sought. My work on dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase is topically close to nucleotide chemistry in B029 and has no bearing on B004. I have no personal or institutional tie to any other shortlisted candidate. My earlier note about B046 is withdrawn now that it is an alternative.
